record_notes.DCP-LETT-1748: August 23 OR September 23, 1855, encoded as two mutually exclusive XML dates; not a continuous month-long range. Sends an unidentified umbellifer for naming. Corrects his own earlier request: one wild celery umbel cannot establish total plant seed yield, so asks for twelve fine whole plants or an explicit estimated total. Has wild/tame carrots and parsnips marked and cabbage/asparagus in hand. Seeks precise facts against two stated naturalists claims about typical forms and cultivated fertility; does not endorse those claims. Later published seed totals are not results already reported here. The uncertain separate-paper postscript now placed with 1712 must not be silently duplicated or assigned to this date.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1765: October 12, supplied 1855. Thanks missing note/programme and reports reading a newspaper account of Hitcham exhibition. Would pay fifty pounds rather than lecture himself; hypothetical expense, not paid. Future review of cirripede collection and conditional whale/turtle parasite specimens are not a shipment. Has lately read an admirable Hooker manuscript on variation and range, but its identity is unresolved: summary confidently names Flora Indica while footnote says possibly an early 1856 essay draft. Do not promote either identification to certainty or manufacture a Hooker incoming source.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1770: October 29, supplied 1855. Peas without parchment and beet arrived some time earlier, not necessarily today. Hooker orally described Paris; the apparatus account of melted wax models is not automatically part of that conversation. Asks Henslow to send collected seeds via Snow at Nags Head, then plans a postal order. Lychnis/Myosotis plants have germinated, but experimental torments begin next spring. Darwin and Emma Glasgow attendance is past; forwarding address and conditional payment remain source prose, not agent actions.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1778: November 10, supplied 1855 heading. Thanks for newly received experimental seeds and encloses ten-shilling postal order. Reports that only one of thirty or forty tested plants remained afloat after a month, while capsicum/celery seeds germinated after 137 days of salt immersion; distinguish flotation from germination and revised expectation from a disproof of all sea transport. Has already sent Vilmorin a note. Lychnis whiteness and counting both parsnip seeds are explicit assumptions pending correction. Requests forwarding hollyhock queries to a grower. The surviving related draft 1779 is dated November 12, so dispatch/assembly cannot safely be set to November 10 solely from heading. Actual dispatched fair copy is unlocated.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1779: November 12, 1855 is written at the end of the draft questions. Recto draft covering letter to Henslow and verso questions are a single draft enclosure associated with 1778, not an incoming Henslow or Chater letter. Questions ask whether kinds come true, whether separation from bees matters, and whether controlled crosses give intermediate colours. These are enquiries and reports of prior authors, not grower answers. Circled inserted a before first question may refer to another intended question; do not invent it or assert final dispatched copy exactly matches draft. Header Nov.— is less complete than closing dateline.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1797: December 18 with supplied month/year. Three blocks acknowledge safely received seeds and refer to Henslow forthcoming busy week. London Friday visit is prospective; footnote records attendance Thursday December 20, which is a distinct event and must not be substituted for the stated plan. No source body for Henslow seed dispatch or schedule survives.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1801: December 26, supplied 1855. Forwards unidentified club book borrowed from Innes and seeks advice about solvency, actuary assessment, withholding future pensions and buying out distant members. Explicitly says the club has not yet granted a pension. Proposed rule and actuarial consultation are not completed actions; no Henslow reply is present. Earlier benefit-club correspondence is background, not this missing answer.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1726: Explicit primary reading reused from accepted batch-12 with unchanged sources. July 21, supplied 1855. Thanks for seeds, lists, programme and fete news, with oral report from the Horners distinct. Reveals the close-species motive: apparently large genera vary more, range more widely and have more numerous individuals. These are qualified observations, not settled facts. Asks about correlated organs and still requests white Lychnis and dried vouchers. Dinner dates are prospective. Later Henslow lessons and book are not contemporary knowledge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1729: Explicit primary reading reused from accepted batch-12 with unchanged sources. July 23 with supplied month and year. Initiates an invitation for August 7 or 8 dinner at seven, with a possible Hooker invitation and request for notice to the cook. No surviving acceptance is identified; do not pair two Darwin outgoing letters.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1732: Explicit primary reading reused from accepted batch-12 with unchanged sources. July 28, supplied 1855. Thanks for missing acceptance and confirms August 7 dinner; offers a bed and says Hooker has been invited, not that he accepted. Thanks for Lychnis, asks for wild celery umbel and a rose seed experiment. Excluded supplemental N.B. is original Darwin prose explaining that the last two letters were misrouted because Kent was omitted. Preserve as attributable authorial text rather than discard all exclusions. It does not establish their exact arrival days. Later August newspaper account and 1868 rose discussion remain apparatus.
